sections.title: Do not die early
sections.intro: This section covers three things: deaths from accidents and injuries such as road crashes, fires, and poisoning; a few vaccines and screenings backed by the strongest evidence; and which bodily signals mean you should get checked. Figures in the Benefit field come from randomized trials, long-term cohort studies, or official statistics. Figures in the Cost field are the author's rough estimates from market prices, for comparison only—not for citation.

entries.title: Always wear seat belts, both front and back
Wearing a helmet and fastening the strap while riding motorcycles or e-bikes
Install smoke alarms; those heating with coal or gas in winter should also add a carbon monoxide alarm
Replace gas hoses and stoves when they reach their expiration date; never modify the piping yourself, and you may decline any unsolicited sales pitches from gas companies
Do not pick, buy, or eat wild mushrooms; any “folk tricks” for identification are useless
Electric bicycles must not be pushed into stairwells, elevators, or charged indoors
Measuring blood pressure and taking meds to reach target levels
After age 35, anyone who is overweight should get a fasting blood glucose test; if the result is normal, repeat it every three years
Don’t speed or drive after drinking
Use a car seat for children under 4, don’t hold them in your arms
Install window guards and balcony barriers if you have kids at home; screen windows do not count as protection
Keep young children in sight near water; wear life jackets when boating or swimming
Exercising balance and leg strength for people over 60, plus home modifications
Get tested for hepatitis B markers; if no antibodies, get vaccinated
If you get pricked by a nail or splinter, or if a wound gets dirty with soil, seek treatment the same day and ask whether a tetanus shot is needed
The earlier women get the HPV vaccine, the better
Breast cancer screening for women: mammograms every two years starting at age 40
For women over 30, HPV testing should be the first choice for cervical cancer screening
Starting colorectal cancer screening at ages 45–50: use fecal immunochemical tests or colonoscopies
People with cardiovascular disease and older adults should get a flu shot each year
Getting the shingles vaccine after age 50
Pneumococcal vaccine for people over 65
Testing for Helicobacter pylori and eradicating it if positive
Heavy smokers should get a low-dose chest CT once a year
Call 12356 if you’re depressed or having suicidal thoughts; don’t keep sleeping pills or pesticides at home
Purchase fire extinguishers, fire blankets, escape respirators, and first-aid kits, then inspect them once a year
Visible blood in urine — even if painless and gone by the next day — still warrants a check-up
If erectile dysfunction appears, check cardiovascular health first — don’t treat it as a purely sexual issue
Weight loss, quitting smoking, and controlling blood pressure and blood sugar can improve erectile function
Always use condoms during sex and never share needles
If you’ve engaged in high‑risk behavior, get tested for HIV — the Chinese CDC offers free testing with full confidentiality
As soon as suicidal thoughts arise, tell someone nearby and hand over those first few minutes
Don’t treat “survival” as a safety net: after ingesting paraquat or inhaling carbon monoxide, emergency care can save lives, but it rarely preserves lung or brain function
Don’t bet on “a few days of rest” after a fall from height: most patients admitted to a trauma ICU survive, though at a cost measured in years
Don’t trade “losing one kidney is no big deal” for cash: the remaining kidney has to do the work of two, and 86% of kidney sellers later say their health got worse
Don’t pick up, disassemble, or sell unidentified metal parts; stay clear of areas marked with the clover symbol
When gambling leads to borrowing money and persistent low mood, call 12356 first and then hand over your bank cards and payment passwords to family members
Men who have sex with men at high risk of HIV infection can significantly lower their infection risk by taking pre-exposure prophylaxis from designated HIV clinics on schedule
Women aged 65 and older should have a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) bone density test; postmenopausal women with osteoporosis risk factors need not wait until 65
If you are diagnosed with osteoporosis, or have fractured from a minor fall, ask a doctor for osteoporosis medication and keep taking it—do not treat calcium supplements as a substitute
Drill holes to measure ice thickness before stepping onto it; don’t go out if it’s under 15 cm thick. Avoid ice over rivers and near ice-fishing holes

sections.title: Don’t die slowly
sections.intro: This section covers just two types of long‑term health risks: those with a big impact on overall mortality and those backed by solid evidence. The items are listed from most cost‑effective to least. A few entries note “randomized trials,” meaning participants were randomly assigned to different groups for comparison — this is the most reliable type of research. All other figures come from observational studies that simply track people over time without any grouping. Such studies produce risk ratios like HR or RR, but they also contain two kinds of confounding factors: participants naturally differ from one another, and some already had health problems before the study began. Therefore these numbers only indicate general trends and approximate magnitudes; they do not guarantee that following these recommendations will produce exactly those results.

entries.title: Quitting smoking, the earlier the better
Don’t smoke at home or in the car, and don’t let guests smoke indoors
Don’t rely solely on willpower to quit smoking — get medication first: success rates more than double
Pick a quit date and stop smoking on that day — don’t taper gradually
Visit a smoking cessation clinic or call 12320 to find local services
Only consider e‑cigarettes if you’ve already tried quitting; non‑smokers should avoid them
Not drinking sugary drinks — even switching to sugar-free ones doesn’t help
Not chewing betel nut
Switch household salt to low‑sodium (potassium‑rich) salt
Brush teeth thoroughly and floss daily; replace missing teeth promptly
Walking 7,000–8,000 steps per day, or accumulating 150–300 minutes of brisk walking each week
People with hypertension and high cholesterol should take their medication regularly as prescribed; never stop on their own
Getting about 7 hours of sleep each night with a consistent schedule
Playing racket sports three times a week for 45 minutes each session
Accumulating brief bouts of strenuous activity like stair climbing or brisk walking to total 4–5 minutes per day
30–60 minutes of strength training per week
Don’t sit for too long at a time — get up and move every now and then
Eat less processed meat (ham, bacon, sausages, luncheon meat)
Drink less or no alcohol
People who drink daily and experience tremors and palpitations when they stop should not try to quit on their own
To drink less, first tally how much you drink each week, then chat briefly with a doctor
Eating a small handful of nuts daily
Swapping some red meat for fish or poultry
Swap some refined rice and flour for whole grains
Drinking tea more than three times a week
Drinking three to four cups of coffee daily, without sugar or cream
Eating 5 servings (about 400 g) of fruits and vegetables daily
Eat fewer ultra-processed foods (chips, instant noodles, pastries, ready meals)
Switching from coal and wood to electricity or gas for cooking and heating
Let hot drinks cool down before drinking; avoid tea, soup, and coffee that are piping hot
Getting some sun during the day — don’t stay out of the light all the time
Keeping BMI between 20–25; losing weight if overweight
Eating chili peppers four or more times per week
Drinking one or two servings of milk or yogurt daily
Eggs need not be avoided, but don’t eat three or four daily
Take baths whenever you can — don’t limit yourself to showers
Keep naps under 30 minutes—no longer than an hour. If you regularly need a one- or two-hour nap to get through the day, it’s time to see a doctor
Catch up on sleep the night after a sleepless night — don’t wait until the weekend
The longer you work night shifts, the higher your cardiovascular risk — switch if you can
Buy pre-packaged cooking oil with an SC code; avoid bulk, unregulated homemade peanut oil
Replacing lard and butter with vegetable oils for cooking: you don’t need to switch oils for health reasons, nor should you expect flaxseed oil to protect your heart
Turn on the range hood while stir-frying and deep-frying, from the moment you light the stove until the cooking is done

sections.title: Don’t waste your energy
sections.intro: This section is all about energy and time. We look at four main factors: how much attention you can actually use each day, how quick your reactions are, how often you make mistakes, and how long it takes you to get back on track after being interrupted. All the numbers here come from direct measurements — either from lab experiments or from tracking large groups of people over time (observational studies). These figures are not converted into life expectancy or mortality rates. Most items in this section carry a B evidence grade; that’s just how this field works, and it doesn’t make the recommendations any less valid. Item 20 deals with what to expect when dealing with police, doctors, or bank tellers; it cites laws rather than experimental data, so its grade is C. Items 15 (treating pessimistic thoughts as symptoms) and 23 (treating the belief that “others expect me to be perfect” as a symptom) use mortality and suicide‑risk figures that follow a different calculation method than the rest of this section, so they’re not compared with the other numbers here.

entries.title: Turn off non‑essential notifications and keep your phone out of sight while working
Keep a fixed wake-up time, even on weekends
Getting 7 to 8 hours of sleep each night — don’t settle for just 6 hours
Avoid caffeine after 2 p.m
Batch-process emails and messages a few times per day
When doing tasks that require continuous thinking, keep out even brief interruptions
Do one thing at a time — don’t reply to messages while in a meeting
Avoid glowing screens one hour before bed; if you must, read paper books or e-ink devices instead
Go to bed at a set time — avoid staying up late for games, short videos, or porn
Don’t make major decisions or send important messages late at night
Take a 10‑minute nap in the afternoon — don’t sleep half an hour
Using earplugs or finding a quiet room for memory-heavy tasks in open offices
Do not work more than 49 hours per week
When you notice yourself endlessly replaying a distressing memory, do something hands‑on instead
Treat thoughts like “things will definitely get worse” as symptoms, not as facts
Cut back on draining relationships and learn to say no to unwanted requests
Walk away when angry; treat the other person as weather, not an enemy
Best low-cost actions when you’re feeling down: move, get sunlight, stick to a schedule, talk to someone, call 12356
Treat police officers, doctors, and bank tellers as rule‑following workers, not as archetypes: paperwork and deadlines — not emotions — drive results
Don’t make “how others are doing” a daily habit: set limits on apps that show peers’ updates or turn them off
When you feel like “everyone saw me make a fool of myself,” cut that estimate in half
Treat “others expect me to be perfect” as a symptom, not a fact
When angry, don’t try to vent by smashing things, punching a bag, or going for a run — first calm your body down
Writing down thoughts and feelings about a troubling issue over several days can be helpful, but don’t expect it to cure anything

sections.title: Don’t waste time
sections.intro: This section is all about time. We look at how many hours you can save each day, week, or year, and how much the odds improve of finishing a task on schedule. We don’t convert time into extra years of life or into money. When money does come up, we only give the calculation method — no final figures. Most of the items here are backed by a single study or overall statistics from time‑use surveys, so the evidence grades are mostly B or C.

entries.title: Write “what to do” as “if… then…”
Write down exit criteria before starting
When deciding whether to continue, only consider future investments and future returns — not what has already been invested
Estimate timelines based on actual time taken in past similar tasks, not on plans
Distribute an agenda beforehand; don’t hold meetings without one; stand if possible
Cut down on meetings – use written asynchronous communication when possible
Break large tasks into subtasks before estimating and starting work
Set a deadline for tasks without an external deadline
Treat procrastination as a way to avoid discomfort, not as a sign of laziness or lack of effort
Keep desired items within reach and unwanted ones out of sight — no need to resist temptation on the spot
Tie your money to your commitment — but first ask if you’re willing to pay
New habits are measured in months, not “21 days”
For those whose procrastination is affecting daily life, self-help materials backed by randomized trials can be effective — no therapist required
Use your own hourly wage to decide which chores to outsource
Set strict daily limits on short‑video and aimless scrolling
Avoiding TV and scrolling news: view information at set times instead
Spend some time learning keyboard shortcuts and automation for common software
When choosing a place to live, prioritize commute time to cut down on one-way travel

sections.title: Don’t waste money
sections.intro: This section is purely about money: how much you can save, how much your yearly returns differ, and what amount you can expect to get back over the long run. None of these figures are converted into years of life or time saved. Entries dealing with investments simply explain how to do the calculations; they rely only on verified historical data and do not constitute any investment advice.

entries.title: Turn off all automatic renewals and switch to manual renewal upon expiry
Conduct the annual tax reconciliation from March to June; be sure to include all eligible special deductions
Housing provident fund isn’t just for buying a home: it can be used for renting, home renovations, and paying property taxes, effective from September 20, 2026 under new regulations
Recalculate your mobile and broadband plans annually: downgrade unused services, and file a complaint if the carrier refuses to comply
Not buying lottery tickets
Walk away the moment you see “high returns,” “guaranteed returns,” or “sure profits”

Avoid making minimum payments on credit cards, and never sign up for installment plans or consumer loans for purchases; if borrowing is unavoidable, first convert the interest rate to an annual percentage rate before comparing options
Don’t give streamers tips, don’t make in‑game purchases, and don’t make impulsive buys
When kids make in-app purchases or send gifts, parents can demand refunds for large sums spent by kids over eight if they never gave consent
Teaching kids one key phrase: anyone who asks them to use a parent’s phone to enter verification codes is a scammer
Skipping extended warranties for electronics
Prefer generic drugs that have passed consistency evaluation and those selected in centralized procurement

Once you set up family medical expense sharing in the yibao app, funds from your individual medical insurance account can be used to pay for your spouse, parents, and children’s medical care and medication
Drinking boiled tap water instead of buying bottled water year-round
Infrequent stock trading
Don’t borrow money to invest, avoid leverage, and never buy assets you don’t understand
Using broad-market index funds instead of actively managed funds as a long-term core holding (the portion of money you keep invested for years)
When picking similar funds, go for those with lower fees
Don’t put all your money into one stock, one platform, or one property

Individuals paying income tax at a rate of 10% or higher can open a private pension account; up to 12,000 yuan per year can be deducted from taxable income. For those paying no tax or only a 3% rate, opening such an account is not worthwhile
Paying for gym visits individually or on short-term plans is only worthwhile if you have a consistent attendance record spanning over a year
Sign a written contract before paying a deposit; if a business faces risks, it must stop taking payments, and you have the right to get back any unused balance if it shuts down
Implementing a 24-hour cooling-off period for non-essential big-ticket purchases; making full use of the seven-day no-questions-asked return policy for online shopping
Don’t fall for “strikethrough prices” or impulse buying during sales
It’s better to choose a non‑return insurance plan and treat any “refunds” or dividends as non‑guaranteed benefits
Get sufficient third‑party liability coverage: the mandatory insurance limits are uniform nationwide and relatively low, so any excess must be paid out of your own pocket
Set aside an emergency fund equal to 3–6 months of living expenses in a readily accessible account
Run a quick comparison before paying off your mortgage — don’t rely on gut feeling
When shopping online, follow platform rules and laws — not influencers or “positive reviews”
If something goes wrong after buying from a livestream, first ask the platform for the seller’s and influencer’s details — they’re required to provide them
If you buy unsafe food, you can demand ten times the purchase price as compensation; if the amount is under 1,000 yuan, you’re still entitled to 1,000 yuan
Check national inspection reports, 3C certification, and energy labels before buying big-ticket items
Bracelets, jade, luxury watches, and collectibles should be judged by “how much you spend” rather than “how much you save”
For jewelry and gemstones, only test reports bearing the CMA mark are acceptable; you must also verify the issuing agency on the regulator’s official website
Random sales such as blind boxes and gacha games are treated as “money that won’t come back”
If you care about what’s in your food, buy pre-packaged products: loose goods at retail counters aren’t legally required to list ingredients
Stocks that have lost value should also be sold according to pre‑set rules — don’t try to even out costs by buying more

Planning to invest in overseas assets such as U.S. stocks? Use QDII funds or the Hong Kong Stock Connect program — don’t open accounts with foreign brokers, and don’t use your annual foreign exchange quota for buying foreign stocks
Only buy insurance for losses your savings can’t cover; use an emergency fund for losses you can afford
If someone at home depends on your income, buy term life insurance for the breadwinner first — not for your kids
Regretting a personal insurance policy signed for over a year? You can cancel it during the cooling-off period and get most of your premium back
Before signing at the bank counter, check whether it’s a deposit or insurance
To cancel your insurance policy, contact the insurer directly — don’t use “policy cancellation agents.” If you feel misled, call 12378 for free assistance
Writing a specific beneficiary on the policy lets family claim the payout: 5 years for life insurance, 2 years for other policies

sections.title: Items to avoid
sections.intro: This section lists products and treatments that *seem* inexpensive and effective at first glance. Yet once you look at the original research, their benefits are practically nonexistent — or even negative. They’re arranged based on two factors: how much money people spend on them and how strong the supporting evidence actually is. The items near the top of the list are the ones you should stop using first.

entries.title: Don’t take multivitamins for longevity or heart protection
Don’t take regular fish oil capsules to prevent heart disease
Don’t give vitamin D supplements to people who already have enough
Don’t take antioxidant supplements to prevent cancer (beta-carotene, vitamin E, vitamin A)
Don’t expect glucosamine/chondroitin to treat knee osteoarthritis
Don’t rely on vitamin C to prevent colds
Don’t get a whole-body PET-CT or tumor marker panel if you have no symptoms
Don’t expect fitness trackers or smartwatches to help you lose weight
Don’t pay a premium for organic food just to be “healthier”
Don’t spend a lot of money on health supplements, herbal formulas, or tonics to “improve your health”
Don’t take probiotics long-term if you have no gut problems
Don’t force yourself to take cold showers just to “boost immunity”
Don’t buy products marketed for detox, colon cleansing, enzymes, or alkaline water
Don’t force yourself to drink water just to hit “8 glasses a day”
Don’t spend money on fortune‑telling, tarot, or astrology to make decisions

Don’t buy blue-light-blocking glasses to “protect your vision,” and don’t believe claims that staring at screens for months will ruin your eyes — but severe eye pain, redness, and swelling require immediate medical attention

Don’t treat blood donation as a health habit: claims that it “detoxifies, lowers cholesterol, and prevents heart attacks” lack randomized trial support, while frequent donation truly causes iron deficiency
Don’t rely on generic health check packages to prevent disease; instead, get the evidence‑based screenings appropriate for your age and gender
Don’t start taking uric‑acid‑lowering drugs just because a checkup shows high uric acid but you’ve never had symptoms
Don’t have a gallbladder removed prophylactically just because an ultrasound found gallstones but you’ve never felt any pain
Don’t cut calcium out to prevent kidney stones
Don’t buy crystals, bracelets, or Pixiu figurines for “good luck,” “wealth attraction,” or “health benefits”
Don’t expect shopping to lift your mood or boost your sense of self-worth
Don’t spend extra money to “move up a rung” among your peers by buying a new house, car, or social circle
Don’t believe that “willpower is like a muscle that runs out after use”
Don’t expect skipping breakfast or the 16:8 intermittent fasting method to help you control your weight; instead, pick a meal timing you can stick to long-term
Don’t believe claims that masturbation harms health or that abstaining improves wellbeing; what really matters is whether it interferes with sleep, work, or relationships
Don’t spend money on “sexual orientation conversion” or “gay conversion therapy,” and don’t send your family members to such programs

sections.title: How to get by when you have little money
sections.intro: This section covers money and social safeguards. It lists how much you might receive, what costs could be waived, which services may be available, and what eligibility criteria apply — but it does not translate these figures into any health impact. Policies change yearly and vary by region, so always refer to the official figures released for your local area. Items are ordered from those requiring no spending, minimal paperwork, and quick results at the top, while those demanding long-term qualification periods or carrying large regional differences appear toward the end. Suggestions based purely on personal experience without any official documentation are placed last.

entries.title: Apply online for unemployment benefits if you’ve lost your job

First file a complaint with the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, then apply for final and binding one-instance arbitration — both options are free, and most cases yield results within a few months
If you can’t afford legal fees, apply for free legal aid – cases involving unpaid wages, alimony, or workplace injuries all qualify
When you have nowhere else to turn, go to a shelter – they provide food, lodging, and even a ticket home
Use free public employment services and gig platforms first — avoid paid agencies
Apply for emergency assistance when unexpected crises occur
Apply for dibao if your household income falls below the local threshold
Apply for the two disability subsidies using a disability certificate
Do not miss the annual 400‑yuan payment for basic medical insurance; subsidies are available for low‑income households
When suffering from a serious illness, first use yibao, dibao, medical assistance, and register for cross‑regional treatment — avoid online loans
Replace a lost ID card immediately; get a temporary ID if you need it urgently
After registering as unemployed, seek recognition as a person facing employment difficulties to receive social insurance subsidies or placement in public-interest jobs
Apply for vocational training subsidies, employment internship subsidies, and social insurance subsidies during unemployment — don’t pay for training courses out of pocket
Job hunting isn’t just about sending resumes — use a systematic approach: learn skills, set goals, and ask for help
No deposits, no ID retention, no “training loans”, no pyramid schemes, no usurious loans
Public rental housing for those with housing difficulties
Keep food and housing costs to a minimum: opt for monthly shared housing instead of daily rentals, and cook at home or use senior meal services rather than ordering takeout
Don’t panic if your social insurance lapses: pension is calculated cumulatively, medical insurance is restored per rules
Even those who have served time, filed for bankruptcy, or ended up on a blacklist still have legal avenues to start over — provided they complete all required procedures
Before facing a serious illness, consider adding a one‑year medical or critical‑illness policy to your basic medical insurance; make sure it includes the phrase “guaranteed renewal”
If there’s nowhere else to sleep, 24‑hour venues can only serve as a temporary overnight stop; shelters should be the first choice

If wages are owed to you, first figure out who actually employed you: unlicensed workshops and labor subcontractors still go through labor inspection; only work for a household or individual as a private helper belongs in court

sections.title: Protect yourself: legal rights and property safety
sections.intro: This section deals with money and personal freedom rather than life expectancy. It covers three main points: what legal responsibilities you must fulfill, how much compensation you can avoid by following those rules, and what procedural rights you have if something goes wrong. All clause numbers have been cross‑checked against the official texts. The items are ordered so that those with the biggest potential losses and the easiest preventive measures appear first; items that require advance planning come next; finally, those based purely on experience without any official backing are listed last.

entries.title: After a traffic accident, stop, help the injured, and call the police — don’t flee
If you realize you’ve been scammed, call 110 or 96110 right away to request a stop‑payment — don’t try to investigate on your own first

Remember the core anti-fraud rules: don’t trust unsolicited calls, don’t share personal information, don’t click on suspicious links, and always verify any transfer requests. All seven of the most common scam types follow this same pattern
Seeing a face on video or hearing a voice on the phone does not count as verification; if a transfer is involved, hang up first and call back using an old number saved in your contacts
If accused or summoned, hire a lawyer first — don’t settle privately or delete records
Coming forward voluntarily after an incident: Self‑surrender can cut a sentence by up to 40%, and the “statute of limitations” defense simply does not exist
Don’t touch the steering wheel after drinking — even for e‑bikes or “just moving the car a bit”
Never lend your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts to anyone — “money laundering” is not a side hustle
Checking your credit report twice a year for free helps spot any loans or cards you didn’t apply for
If a fight breaks out, call the police first — the one who strikes first almost always loses
You may defend yourself against an unavoidable attack, but only strike the person who is actually attacking — stop when he stops
Who to hold accountable — unpaid wages, wrongful dismissal, financial losses — filing complaints, arbitration, or lawsuits instead of taking revenge

No matter how angry you are, never target innocent people: deliberately driving into a crowd or committing violence in public is classified as endangering public safety by dangerous means, carrying a minimum sentence of three years; if anyone dies, the penalty is death
Thoughts such as “find a scapegoat” or “die together” must be treated as a medical emergency: leave the scene, hand over car keys and knives to someone else, and call 12356

Family members say “no one will be safe” or “I’ll take the kids and leave” — don’t dismiss this as anger: close relatives can take such a person to the hospital, and police must respond to any emergency call
Don’t curse, spread rumors, or share unverified content online; if you’re a victim of online abuse, document evidence first then report it to police
Read the document thoroughly before signing; never sign on behalf of others or on blank paper
Write a clear loan agreement when lending money; think carefully before agreeing to be a guarantor
Time limits for legal action: 3 years for civil lawsuits, 1 year for labor arbitration; once the deadline passes, a simple “statute of limitations exceeded” claim can block your case
If you’re being sued or have a court order against you, report all your assets truthfully and repay as much as you can — don’t transfer your house or money to relatives, friends, or companies
If you’re subject to spending restrictions or listed on the dishonesty registry, first find out which rule applies and request removal if possible
If scammed while shopping online or via second-hand markets, first file a complaint with the platform, then report it to police, and finally decide whether to sue
Think carefully before and after making large gifts in romantic relationships or marriage
Transfer betrothal gifts via payment with clear notes; keep chat records; money demanded under marriage can be reclaimed
No need to worry about premarital assets — clearly define property additions and parental contributions
Check a person’s marital status before getting married; those who use marriage as a pretext to defraud money can be prosecuted for fraud
For home appliance repairs, vehicle inspections, and renovations: always ask for a quote first and stay on site throughout the process
Don’t be a “nominal legal representative” — don’t lend your ID to register a company
Don’t carry items for strangers when traveling, and don’t accept packages of unknown origin
Leashing dogs is mandatory: failure to do so means strict liability for any harm caused (you must pay compensation regardless of fault), and the obligation extends fully
If the other person is intoxicated, unconscious, or under 14, do not have sex with them
If someone threatens to call the police, post intimate photos, or inform your workplace unless you pay up — don’t give them a single cent and don’t delete any records; call the police right away
If someone falsely accuses you, you can seek legal consequences: up to 5 days of detention for minor violations, up to 3 years in prison for criminal acts
Insufficient evidence alone warrants acquittal; coerced confessions must be excluded; appeals and retrials remain possible after conviction

For individuals released from detention after a case is dropped, charges are withdrawn, or they are acquitted, applying for state compensation is possible — compensation is calculated on a daily basis

If you’re a victim seeking compensation, use channels like 12315, file a lawsuit, or hire a lawyer. Never meet the offending party alone, and don’t phrase “paying money” and “I won’t expose you” as a single condition
Cyberbullying: First enable protections, gather evidence, then choose between court injunctions, private prosecution, or police reports

The legal route of “buying insurance for a family member first, then harming them” is completely blocked: you get zero money, and the perpetrator faces multiple charges including intentional homicide and insurance fraud

You must obtain a case receipt when reporting a crime; if no case is opened, you must receive a written notice. You can request a reconsideration within 7 days and a review within another 7 days. The procuratorate can also order the police to open a case
Don’t give money or cards to investigators, law enforcers: offering bribes is a crime, and bribing oversight, law enforcement, and judicial staff is punished even more severely
For calls and in-person talks where things might turn sour, start recording right away: you can record conversations you personally take part in without needing prior consent from the other party
In an emergency at the scene, first film a wide shot, then capture the spatial relationships, and finally record the damage and injuries — keep the original photos and videos
Domestic violence: Call the police to get an incident report, then apply to court for a protection order — no divorce required and it’s free
Family members have gambling debts — don’t rush to pay them: gambling debts aren’t legally protected, nor are loans taken for gambling considered joint marital debts

Don’t agree when an acquaintance asks you to “help by doing a facial scan or acting as a witness” to secure a loan, or to read out a verification code — this is known as “AB loan” fraud. In this scheme, you are the borrower, not a guarantor

sections.title: Legal pitfalls that ordinary people often overlook
sections.intro: This section looks at two key aspects: personal freedom and money. Many everyday actions that people assume are harmless can actually lead to detention, fines, or even criminal sentences. For each item we list the exact legal numbers from statutes, along with real cases documented by official sources. The Public Security Administration Punishment Law referenced here is the 2025 revised version, which took effect on January 1, 2026; its article numbers differ from earlier editions. The Criminal Law excerpts come from a compiled text reposted by Beijing’s Traffic Management Bureau, updated according to Amendment XI to the Criminal Law; we note which amendment applies to each passage. Items are ordered from those most likely to be unintentionally broken to those carrying the heaviest penalties.

entries.title: Do not share unverified messages about disasters, epidemics, or police incidents in groups; do not photoshop images or use AI to generate fake scene pictures
Do not post, share, or comment images, memes, or remarks that insult heroes and martyrs, nor make jokes about the national flag or anthem
After viewing content on foreign websites, simply close the page — do not screenshot, share, repost, or discuss it in any groups or comment sections
Watching porn alone is fine, but don’t post it in groups, sell “resources,” or create groups
Part-time jobs that ask you to use your own card to receive payments, withdraw cash, or transfer money — no matter how much extra pay they offer, avoid them
Some people try to get you to “package loan applicants” for them and offer a commission based on the loan amount — don’t fall for it
Keeping found items and not using them for personal gain; returning lost phones, wallets, or cash to owners or police
Use your real identity to claim discounts — don’t register fake accounts or exploit loopholes to get more
Never throw anything from balconies or windows — cigarette butts, trash bags, and bottles all count
Do not buy imitation guns, BB guns, or air rifles online; avoid “toy guns” of unknown origin
Register drones with your real name first; never fly near airports, military zones, or restricted urban airspace, and don’t tamper with altitude limits
Do not secretly film others, nor install cameras in rented apartments, homestays, or hotel rooms
Mahjong and poker can be played — no rake, no banker role, no organizing paid games, no online gambling
Do not eat wild animals; do not buy, sell, or keep protected species as pets
You cannot detain or confine someone to collect a debt, nor follow them home and refuse to leave
Do not lend your ID card, do not use someone else’s ID card, and do not register, open accounts, or buy tickets using another person’s documents
Cooperate when stopped or taken away by police — don’t push, hit, or grab their body cameras; especially if you’ve been drinking, stay calm
Sexual relations with anyone under 14 are illegal; “she consented” is not a defense
Do the math before you hit someone: detention, fines, and prison time

If parents cannot care for their newborn, the only legal option is to register the adoption with the civil affairs bureau: paying someone to hand over the child may be prosecuted as child trafficking, while abandoning the child constitutes abandonment
Don’t fabricate accidents or exaggerate damages to defraud insurance payouts: this is insurance fraud, and anyone helping you testify, assess damage, or repair your vehicle is equally liable

Don’t sell your own organs, and don’t help others find donors: a kidney brings in just over $20,000, but the same kidney can be sold to a patient for $200,000. All proceeds are seized, plus a fine of 10–20 times the transaction amount
Don’t engage in prostitution: the default penalty is 10–15 days in detention, not just a fine

Distributing unauthorized Chinese-dubbed comics, pirated movies/TV shows, cloud storage links, and pirated e-books — even for free — is illegal; adding ads or charging membership fees can lead to criminal charges
To publish or monetize fan works, first obtain permission from the original copyright holder, or replace the borrowed characters’ names and relationships with your own

sections.title: Is it worth dating and getting married?
sections.intro: This section breaks down the question “Is marriage a good financial decision?” into several separate calculations. These calculations cover money, time, health, legal risks, and relationship quality. For each calculation we use only figures with verifiable sources — primarily official statistics or meta-analyses that combine data from multiple studies. No moral judgments are made here, nor are any conclusions drawn on your behalf. The health calculations rely on mortality risks, the time calculations use average daily minutes, and the legal calculations follow the wording of relevant statutes. These three types of calculations are not converted into one another. For more details on this breakdown method, the checklist of factors to consider, and common misconceptions, please refer to [docs/结婚划不划算.md](../../docs/research/结婚划不划算.md).

entries.title: Getting to know more people rather than fixating on just one: You can’t predict compatibility before meeting someone
Stop after a clear refusal — continued pursuit is a public order violation, not “sincerity”
Judging whether someone is interested: focus on actions, not “signals” — who initiates, plans, and follows up
Whether a relationship is good or not depends mainly on how you feel within it, not on your partner’s attributes
To build closeness, have two people take turns answering a series of progressively deeper questions — no script needed
Long-distance relationships aren’t worse than local ones — the real challenge comes in the first three months after moving in together
Check registration statistics before listening to elders: what do “marriage rate” and “divorce rate” actually mean?
Accounting for health benefits while adjusting for observational data
Discussing labor division before marriage helps clarify unpaid work responsibilities
First check the default legal rules regarding money and property, then decide whether to make a written agreement
When parents pay for a house, they should clearly state whether it’s a loan or a gift at the time of transfer
Money borrowed by a spouse in a large amount — if you didn’t sign or later acknowledge it, it doesn’t automatically become your debt
Obtaining a marriage certificate requires only an ID card and a signed declaration — no household register needed, no fees, and issuance is immediate
Undergoing a premarital medical exam: if a serious illness is present, it must be disclosed before marriage registration
Calculating the cost of walking away: Divorce by mutual agreement requires a 30-day cooling-off period, while divorce via litigation has strict legal prerequisites
Make a separate tally for the benefits to your elders when they get married — don’t mix it with your own records
Treating relationship quality as a health factor: focus on the issue, not the person — avoid insults and sarcasm

Same-sex partners should prepare a power of attorney, a voluntary guardianship agreement, and a will while both are still lucid: legally, you are not considered close relatives, so without these documents you’ll have no right to sign on behalf of each other or to inherit anything
Don’t marry while hiding your sexual orientation, and don’t treat “marriage of convenience” as an easy shortcut: legally, it is a real marriage, and the only way out is divorce
When a relationship is stuck in endless arguments and silent treatment, couples therapy can help — waiting alone rarely does

sections.title: Common legal pitfalls for programmers and tech professionals
sections.intro: This section focuses on personal freedom and financial safety — essentially, avoiding imprisonment and costly lawsuits. Many developers and technical workers tend to treat the following issues as mere technical matters. In reality, they constitute specific criminal offenses under Chinese law or can lead to substantial civil liabilities. For each item, we list the relevant legal provisions and real-world cases published on the websites of the Supreme People’s Procuratorate and the Supreme People’s Court. The criminal law references come from a consolidated text republished by the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau, which reflects amendments introduced in the 11th Criminal Law Amendment. The items are ordered from those most likely to be underestimated by tech professionals to those with the most severe consequences. The first entry serves as a general guide: it explains how to assess risks before taking action and what steps to take immediately after any incident occurs.

entries.title: Ask three questions before taking any action: Whose interests might be harmed? How capable is the other party of pursuing legal action? And how much evidence do I have? If legal action is taken, immediately hire a criminal defense attorney
Refraining from creating or selling game cheats and aids, including AI tools that only capture screenshots without touching memory
Do not write or sell scripts for ticket snatching, flash sales, fake orders, or coupon farming — even if they merely “automate button clicks”

The crawler only accesses publicly available pages that require no login; it does not attempt to bypass anti-scraping measures or handle any personal information, and any data it collects is never sold
Refuse development orders for gambling, fraud, or adult-content apps; do not set up payment gateways or unblock accounts for such “clients”
Upon leaving a job, return all account access rights; do not delete databases, leave backdoors, or alter password protection systems — even if the employer owes you wages
Do not take source code, client lists, or technical documents upon leaving; do not upload them to personal cloud drives or reuse them at new employers
Do not run your own programs on others’ computers, servers, or cameras; do not use company machines for mining
Testing someone else’s systems without written permission — “good intentions” and “reporting afterward” are not excuses
Vulnerabilities must be reported per regulations; no details, exploit tools, or disclosure to foreign entities before patching
No selling of tools for bypassing firewalls or VPN accounts, no setting up such nodes for others

After signing a non-compete agreement, if the employer fails to pay compensation monthly, send a written notice; if payment still doesn’t come after 3 months, you may terminate the agreement. Workers who never handled any trade secrets can request that the clause be declared invalid
Code written during work hours using company resources belongs to the company; personal open‑source projects should be done in your own time and on your own equipment, without mixing them
Using open-source code such as GPL in products: Open-source it per the license or switch licenses — don’t treat this as “no one cares”
Only collect personal data strictly necessary for the app’s operation; consent from guardians is required for users under 14, and the privacy policy must be clearly written
Before launching a website or app, complete ICP registration and retain logs for at least 6 months per classification protection requirements
Before offering generative AI services to the public, conduct required safety assessments and algorithm registration; mark all generated content

sections.title: Starting a business: how to protect your personal assets
sections.intro: This section deals with money and legal liability. What steps could potentially put your own savings, your family’s money, and even your spouse’s funds at risk when opening a shop or forming a company? What does the law say about this? Is it possible to set up safeguards in advance? This section answers those questions without trying to convert the risks into life‑years lost. The items are ordered from the scenarios that most easily threaten personal assets to those that are easiest to avoid. Consequently, items that require only a signature come first, while methods that demand hands‑on effort appear later. Any statements based purely on experience and lacking supporting research are marked as Grade C evidence.

entries.title: Only invest money you can afford to lose — never use family savings or borrowed funds
Never sign personal guarantees for corporate loans; spouses should definitely avoid signing too
Choosing the right legal entity before launching: sole proprietors and general partners are fully liable, while limited liability companies offer “limited” liability
Improperly listed shareholders: never hold shares on someone else’s behalf
Check the Ministry of Commerce records before signing; obtain written disclosures and include a “cooling-off period” in the contract
Determine the business name, location, scope of operations, and registered capital before registration; with complete documents, you can obtain the business license on the spot
Businesses requiring licenses must wait until they obtain one
Figure out which category you fall into: producing or preparing food requires a permit, selling only pre-packaged goods needs a filing, while selling fresh meat and vegetables needs no permit at all
Packaging food for sale makes it prepackaged food: labels must include production date, shelf life, and ingredient list without exception
General foods must not claim therapeutic effects: this applies to labels, instructions, ads, and live-stream scripts alike

The food industry faces criminal penalties: selling meat from diseased animals or products exceeding safety limits is already a crime; adding toxic or harmful non-food substances carries a minimum five-year sentence regardless of revenue
Once you obtain a business license, you must file tax returns on schedule — even if you have no income, you still need to submit a return with all zeros
Invoices must reflect actual transactions; small taxpayers can fully utilize tax exemptions
Scammers pretending to be tax officials demanding payments are fraudsters; tax filings must be done via the e-Tax Service or by calling 12366
Writing “deposit” instead of “advance payment” in contracts, specifying penalty amounts, and treating credit terms as loans
Sign a written contract within the first month of employment; register for social insurance within 30 days
Wages must be paid according to contracts and laws; raises, loans, and bonuses all require written documentation
Sell first, then produce: use pre-orders and small orders to confirm demand before investing in manufacturing
Run the prototype through the production checklist before starting full production

Keep copies of invoices and supplier documentation for every shipment; avoid purchasing goods priced significantly below market rates: if an employee buys counterfeit products, the employer can still be held legally responsible
Whether creating designs yourself or purchasing licensed artwork, simply changing colors or adding icons does not count as “modifications” for copyright purposes
Follow procedures at work; think carefully about who bears responsibility before offering unsolicited help
Exit the process as planned when losses occur: opt for simplified deregistration when possible, or file for bankruptcy if debts exceed assets — don’t leave things unattended
Before paying for third‑party store management, e‑commerce training, or “dropshipping” services, be sure to ask whether extra fees will be required and where the sales figures actually come from

sections.title: Emergency situations: what to do first
sections.intro: This section covers just one thing: what actions you should take right away when an emergency occurs, what to do next, and what to avoid. The entries on first aid and wilderness survival focus on specific causes of death and survival rates. Those dealing with scams and threats involve financial loss and threats to personal freedom. These two sets of figures cannot be compared with each other. Entries are ordered by how common each situation is and how much difference proper or improper action can make in terms of lives saved. These guidelines are primarily meant for you, your spouse, and close family members. In fact, 79.2% of cardiac arrests happen at home, so the people you’re most likely to help are your household members, followed by friends and coworkers. While helping strangers can also be worthwhile, it ranks last in priority due to risks such as false accusations or getting involved in legal trouble. Therefore, the entries in this category emphasize actions to protect yourself and include clauses that limit your liability. Only actions that must be taken within a few minutes are included here. Identifying scams or dealing with extortion attempts require longer-term measures and are not covered in this section. Detailed anti-fraud rules and descriptions of seven common types of fraud can be found in Section 8, Item 3. Information on handling situations where someone threatens to release private photos or intimate videos is provided in Section 8, Item 32. If money has already been transferred, you should immediately call 110 or 96110 to request a stop payment, as explained in Section 8, Item 2.

entries.title: Immediate chest compressions can save lives when someone collapses and stops breathing — call 120 and fetch an AED too

Elderly falls: if someone falls, first kneel down, call out to them, and dial 120 — don’t rush to help them up. It is perfectly legal to walk away from strangers; once you stop, however, you must not touch or move them
Sudden facial drooping, weakness in one arm, and slurred speech — call 120 immediately; don’t wait or drive yourself
Sudden dizziness, double vision, loss of vision in one eye, or inability to touch one’s nose — all warrant calling 120 for stroke suspicion
One eye suddenly goes dark, as if a curtain has been pulled shut; even if it clears up within minutes, seek emergency care for stroke on the same day
One eye is swollen, painful, red; there’s a rainbow halo around lights; plus headache, nausea, and vomiting — so an emergency eye visit is needed that same day
Chest pressure, tightness, or heaviness lasting more than 15 minutes without relief — call 120; do not drive yourself
Sudden tearing pain that spreads from the chest to the back and waist — call 120 and describe it as “pain moving downward”
A sudden “worst headache of one’s life” that peaks within an hour — go to the ER for a head CT right away

After an elderly person suffers a head injury, they may develop unsteady gait, sluggishness, excessive sleepiness, or weakness on one side of the body two to three weeks later — a CT scan is recommended
A leg suddenly swells, feels tight, and is tender to the touch — seek medical care promptly; if shortness of breath or chest pain develops suddenly, call 120 immediately
For severe bleeding, first press firmly on the wound with your hand; if this fails on limbs, apply a tourniquet and call 120 immediately
For dog or cat bites and scratches, rinse the area with soap and running water for 15 minutes, then get vaccinated on the same day
Immediately rinse a burn with cool running water for 20 minutes; avoid applying toothpaste or soy sauce
Sudden widespread rash, difficulty breathing, or dizziness — treat as anaphylactic shock; call 120 immediately and explain the situation clearly
Someone is having a seizure — clear the area, place them on their side, time the episode, and don’t put anything in their mouth
Diabetic patients suddenly start shaking, break out in cold sweats, and have slurred speech — first give 15 grams of sugar, then retest after 15 minutes
If someone is electrocuted, cut the power first, then use a dry wooden stick to pry the source of electricity away; never pull the victim by hand directly
If a carbon monoxide alarm goes off, or if several people in a room suddenly get headaches, nausea, or dizziness, get everyone outside before calling for help

If someone accidentally ingests detergent, pesticides, or medicine, do not induce vomiting — take the container and seek medical help right away; if it splashes into the eyes or onto the skin, rinse thoroughly with water for at least 15 minutes

In case of splashes of acids, alkalis or other chemicals on the body, immediately remove contaminated clothing and rinse with copious amounts of running water; for eyes, gently pull the eyelids apart and rinse thoroughly before leaving the scene

Dizziness, nausea, lack of sweating or confusion in high heat — move to shade immediately, remove clothing and apply cool water to cool down; do not give water to anyone who is unconscious, call 120 right away

For people suffering from heatstroke, as long as they remain conscious, they should drink small amounts of cool, lightly salted water or sports drinks at frequent intervals — never gulp down large quantities. Alcohol and sugary drinks must be avoided
Stay low to the ground during a fire, test doors before opening them, and never use elevators — once outside, don’t look back
Upon seeing someone drowning, shout for help and call 110/120, then reach out a pole or floating objects — never enter the water yourself
If someone is choking and can’t speak, stand behind them and perform 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts; if they collapse, start CPR immediately

If lost or stranded in the Gobi Desert, a desert, or any remote area, stay put next to your vehicle. First, transmit your location, then shield yourself from the sun and retain body heat, conserve water, and avoid wandering off
Shivering, slurred speech, and unsteady walking are signs of hypothermia; change into dry clothes, wrap up, warm the torso first, and give sweet hot drinks instead of alcohol
After a snake bite, stay still, remove rings and watches, and rush to a hospital offering antivenom — no cutting, no suction, no tight binding

First, figure out what kind of building you’re in during an earthquake: if it meets seismic safety standards, stay right where you are; if it’s an old structure prone to collapse, head outside right away
When encountering bears, wild boars, or packs of wild dogs, don’t run, don’t scream, don’t make eye contact — instead, turn sideways and back away slowly
If caught in a thunderstorm outdoors, get into a hard-topped vehicle or building; avoid ridges, lone trees, water surfaces, and metal objects
Gradually increase your sleeping altitude when heading to high elevations; if symptoms worsen, descend immediately — don’t tough it out
To remove a tick, use fine-point tweezers to pull it straight out along the skin — don’t apply oil, don’t use heat
Always boil any water taken from the wild before drinking it; one minute of boiling is sufficient — there’s no need to extend the time just because you’re at high altitude
If a stranger demands money in a remote area, hand over cash, avoid any confrontation, note their features, and call police after escaping

If you stumble upon a group fight, walk away immediately — don’t try to break it up, don’t stand around watching, and don’t pick up any weapons on the ground. If you want to call the police, retreat to a safe distance and dial 110
If you may have been exposed to HIV, get PEP within 72 hours — the sooner, the better
After saving someone and getting injured or incurring expenses, first seek compensation from the perpetrator and yibao; then apply for recognition as a person acting in the public interest
Knives, rebar, glass piercing the body – apply pressure around the foreign object to stop bleeding; do not pull it out
If a fracture is suspected, don’t move the injured area — keep it supported and apply cold for up to 20 minutes; never try to realign it yourself
After sexual assault, go to a safe place and call 110; do not shower, wash clothes, or tidy the room before a medical exam, and visit a hospital within 72 hours
When a baby under 1 year is choking and cannot cry out, alternate 5 back blows (face-down) and 5 chest thrusts — never press the belly
If a baby under 1 is unresponsive and not breathing normally, call 120 on speakerphone and perform infant CPR: 30 compressions, then 2 breaths

sections.title: Account and Information Security
sections.intro: Backlink: Protecting your money and personal data is essential. If someone gains access to your accounts, they can steal funds right away. They may also use your account to scam people on your contact list. In short, your identity becomes vulnerable too.

entries.title: Enable two-factor authentication on email, payment, and social accounts; prioritize phone pop-ups over SMS codes
Use a unique password solely for your email
Set a screen lock on your phone and a PIN for the SIM card
Follow these steps if you lose your phone: block the SIM card, remotely lock it, change passwords, file a police report, and freeze your bank cards if needed
If your card is fraudulently used, report it and freeze the card first, then demand compensation from the bank: proving “you made the transaction” is the bank’s responsibility
Periodically check the devices logged into your account and any authorized apps, then remove the ones you no longer use
Don’t tap “Allow all” just to use an app: the data isn’t mandatory, and refusing to share it won’t block service access
You have the right to view, copy, correct, and delete your personal information; if refused, you can sue
You’re not required to use facial recognition: if other options exist, they must offer you alternatives if you refuse

sections.title: Renting vs. buying a home
sections.intro: Renting can easily cost you extra due to security deposits and realtor fees. Buying a home, on the other hand, brings high expenses in the form of mortgage interest and all those hidden details that sellers know but buyers often overlook.

entries.title: The amount of the deposit, its refund timeline, and permissible deduction scenarios must be specified in the contract
When water and electricity are cut off, locks are changed, or you’re threatened to leave — call the police right away: laws forbid using these tactics to force you out
Real estate agents must not collect or remit rent and security deposits; payments go straight to landlords
Check a long-term rental’s escrow account before paying a full year’s rent upfront
House sold during lease term – lease remains valid, no need to move
Checking property rights and mortgages before signing the contract; all payments must be transferred with a purpose note
For second-hand home sales where the agent collects the payment, the funds must be deposited into a dedicated transaction account opened by the agency at a bank
Don’t rent a subdivided apartment: the smallest legal rental unit is the original room as designed; kitchens, bathrooms, balconies must not be used for living
Urban residents with hukou who want to live in the countryside can only rent rural houses — they must not buy homestead land or houses on it

sections.title: How to live after being diagnosed with a chronic disease
sections.intro: This section looks at overall mortality rates and the associated costs. A chronic disease diagnosis is not the end of the story — what truly matters is how to manage it over the decades that follow.

entries.title: Take medication exactly as prescribed — don’t stop just because you feel better

First get outpatient chronic disease certification, then register for cross-regional medical care — hypertension, diabetes, cancer radiotherapy/chemotherapy, dialysis, and anti-rejection treatment can then be covered by yibao across regions
Follow the intervals recommended by your doctor for follow‑up visits, and record every measurement in the same notebook
Don’t stop proper treatment to try folk remedies or supplements
For patients with stable chronic conditions, community clinics can issue up to 12 weeks’ worth of medication at one time
Before signing up for a family doctor in your community, find out which services are covered by yibao and which you’ll have to pay for out of pocket
Get a dilated eye exam right after a diabetes diagnosis, then follow your doctor’s recommended schedule; check your feet once a year
People who have had kidney stones should drink 2.5–3 liters of water daily and keep salt intake under 6 grams
Long‑term use of uric‑acid‑lowering drugs after a gout diagnosis to keep levels below 360 µmol/L

sections.title: Having elderly family members at home
sections.intro: Having elderly relatives living with you often means that the main problems aren’t a lack of money, but failing to discuss matters clearly and sign the necessary documents in advance. The final section looks at pressure ulcers in bedridden patients; it calculates costs based on mortality rates and isn’t meant to be compared with the other items in this chapter.

entries.title: While the elderly are still lucid, designate a future guardian in writing
Make a will — remember that later ones override earlier ones, and notarized wills no longer take priority
Keep the elderly person’s money in a separate account and set a rule requiring two people to approve any large withdrawals
A ready-made phrase for seniors to deflect unwanted offers

Avoid any “investment-based senior care” schemes that require upfront payments: card enrollment, prepaid care fees, buying senior housing units, travel-based care programs, and sales of senior products all fall under the same category of illegal fundraising
Apart from the housing reverse mortgage insurance offered by insurers, you should avoid all other “housing-for-pension” schemes — never mortgage your home to buy financial products
For elderly individuals at home who are bedridden or severely disabled, apply to the local yibao (basic medical insurance) office for long-term care insurance; it is not limited to seniors only
For families with someone bedridden at home, pressure ulcers are a top concern: use an electric alternating-pressure air mattress, turn the patient regularly, and check bony areas daily
If an older person’s cataracts already affect walking safely, have an eye doctor assess surgery; when both eyes are affected, do not delay the second eye too long

sections.title: Is raising a child worth it?
sections.intro: This section breaks down the financial and time costs involved. Much like Section 10, which examined the costs of marriage, we’re simply laying out the numbers here — without offering any definitive conclusions. If you’re already pregnant and need to follow the necessary steps, please refer to Section 27. There are 18 key considerations to keep in mind when deciding whether raising a child is worthwhile.

entries.title: Start by claiming what you’re entitled to: the national dibao program gives 3,600 yuan per child per year until the child turns 3
Maternity leave lasts 98 days; maternity benefits are paid by the maternity insurance fund based on the employer’s average monthly wage from the prior year
Important to know: Employers cannot cut pay or fire workers due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding
The time-cost calculation is based on “whose time is being used,” not on “how hard it is”
Breaking down costs into three periods: ages 0–3, compulsory education, and post‑compulsory education
Keep separate accounts for having kids for your elders, for marriage, and for old-age security

sections.title: While employed, upon leaving the job, and for work‑related injuries
sections.intro: This section is all about money — how it’s calculated, what paperwork you must sign, and what deadlines apply. The first three items cover payments you’re entitled to while still on the payroll. The next six items deal with situations after you leave your job. Finally, the last seven items address occupational diseases and work‑related injuries. Compensation for injuries is far higher than severance pay, and the time limits are much stricter. Unfortunately, damage caused by an occupational disease can never be fully reversed.

entries.title: Overtime pay is calculated at three rates: 1.5×, 2×, and 3× the regular wage; failure to pay warrants a complaint to labor authorities, and non‑payment after the deadline incurs an additional penalty of 50%–100% of the owed amount
Annual leave is calculated based on total years of service: 5, 10, or 15 days. If unused, employees receive 300% of their daily wage as compensation
There is a legal limit on probation periods, wages must be at least 80% of the regular rate, and only one probation period may be set per employee
Calculating N: One month’s salary per full year of service; half a month for periods under six months
If a company fires you without 30 days’ notice, it must pay an extra month’s salary
When a company unlawfully terminates employment, the compensation equals twice the standard severance amount
Never sign “voluntary resignation for personal reasons”; doing so forfeits your entitlements
Save pay stubs, attendance records, employment contracts, social insurance documents, and chat logs before leaving your job

Before taking up a post where there is dust, noise, or chemicals, check whether the contract mentions any occupational hazards; the employer must arrange and pay for three occupational health examinations
Damage caused by dust, noise, and chemical toxins is irreversible: employers must provide protective gear, and workers can refuse unsafe tasks
If you’re injured at work or hit while commuting, the first step is to get a work‑injury determination; if your employer won’t file it, you must do it yourself
Don’t believe the myth that “staying at work counts as a workplace injury”: if you suddenly feel unwell, call 120 first — don’t rush to clock in
Even if the employer fails to enroll you in workers’ compensation insurance, you still qualify for full benefits paid entirely by the employer at the same rates
After injuries stabilize, undergo a work capacity assessment; disability grades translate directly into compensation
Three types of compensation for work-related deaths: funeral allowance, survivor’s pension, and one-time death benefit
If you’ve been bullied, insulted, or mistreated at work for a long time, don’t just endure it: document everything as evidence, then take action based on the nature of the abuse
When you leave a job, ask the employer for a termination certificate stating contract term, separation date, position, and years of service

Before spending severance pay, check individual income tax: amounts within three times the local prior-year average employee wage are tax-free; the excess is taxed separately, not merged into that year’s salary

sections.title: How to care for a newborn baby
sections.intro: This section focuses on two main topics: what it takes to keep a newborn alive and how much it will cost you. Only differences that are substantial and backed by solid evidence are included here. Detailed advice on soothing or raising a baby is beyond the scope of this book. For tasks to handle before birth and on the day of discharge, please refer to Section 27.

entries.title: Keep infants sleeping on their backs on a firm surface; share a room but not a bed; and do not place any soft items in the crib or bed
Administer the first dose of hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours after birth
Ensure your child receives all vaccines in the national immunization schedule at no cost; missed doses can be added later
Breastfeed exclusively for the first 6 months — no water needed; introduce solids at 6 months while continuing breastfeeding
Use water hotter than 70 °C to prepare formula, then let it cool before feeding; discard any leftovers
Do not feed honey to children under 1 year old
Vitamin K injection at birth is essential
Infants under 3 months with a body temperature of 38°C should be taken straight to the hospital — no home observation needed
No matter how tired or angry you are, never shake a baby
When choosing diapers, focus on three things: fit, how often you change them, and whether they’ve been flagged in any quality inspections
Consider buying big-ticket items in the order “borrow, buy used, buy new” — don’t buy them all at once
For children with severe eczema or egg allergy, don’t avoid peanuts — introduce them early under medical guidance, but never feed whole peanuts
Watch newborn jaundice for these signals: yellow within 24 hours of birth, getting yellower, hard to wake or refusing feeds, pale stools — go to hospital the same day

sections.title: Traveling abroad, trips, and safety overseas
sections.intro: This section deals with both financial matters and personal freedom, and several points also relate to physical safety. Once you’re overseas, it’s the laws of the host country that apply — not Chinese law. There are clear limits to what China’s embassies and consulates can do to assist you. This section explains those limits in detail.

entries.title: Check the Ministry of Foreign Affairs safety advisories before you travel; steer clear of any locations marked “Do Not Travel”

Save the 12308 hotline number and your local embassy/consulate’s consular protection number in your phone, then write them down and keep a copy in your wallet — don’t wait until an emergency to look them up
Understanding what consular protection can and cannot do: it can visit you, but cannot bail you out, and you still have to pay the costs
Purchase insurance covering overseas medical care and medical evacuation — don’t settle for just flight delay coverage
Treat all “high-paying overseas jobs” as scams — getting caught can lead to a 6‑month to 3‑year travel ban
The annual limit of 100,000 RMB for cash withdrawals abroad applies to all cards under your name combined
Take photos of your passport, visa, and ID card and store them in the cloud; if lost, report to police first and then apply for a travel document
Before driving abroad, verify whether local authorities recognize Chinese driver’s licenses; most “international driver’s permits” sold online are legally worthless
When hiring an agency for visas, study abroad, or immigration, first check whether it is registered with immigration authorities
Don’t issue invitation letters for strangers, and don’t let others use your name for immigration paperwork
Before traveling abroad, send your itinerary, accommodation details, and travel companions’ information to a family member, and agree on how often you’ll stay in touch

sections.title: How to relax: entertainment venues and stress relief
sections.intro: This section is divided into two parts. The first part covers entertainment venues — it explains which costs are unnecessary and where the emergency exits are located. The focus here is on money and personal freedom. The second part discusses ways to relieve stress, with an emphasis on energy levels and overall mortality risk. The figures from each part are not combined for any calculations. Section 3 already listed several steps to take when feeling down; this section provides more detailed recommendations.

entries.title: Check where the emergency exits are before entering a KTV, bar, or escape room; if they’re locked or blocked, pick another venue
Price lists must be displayed before ordering; entertainment venues cannot charge “after the fact”
If someone offers you “stuff” at a venue, leave immediately — harboring and providing both count as aiding friends
Don’t accept candy or snacks from strangers, don’t drink beverages left unattended, and don’t take e‑cigarette cartridges handed to you by others
Avoid scripted-murder-mystery (剧本杀, "jubensha") and escape rooms located in residential buildings or below the first basement level
Going for a brisk walk or a jog when feeling down: the effect size of exercise on depression is proportional to its intensity
When anxiety interferes with daily life, mindfulness‑based stress reduction works just as well as common anti‑anxiety drugs
For quick relief on the spot, try the 5‑minute “cyclic sigh”: two inhalations followed by a prolonged exhalation
Treat “regular social contact” as a health expense — don’t wait until you’re feeling down to reach out
Living near green spaces means you can use them for walking, strolling, or just sitting around

sections.title: Which skills are worth learning?
sections.intro: This section deals with money and time. The second item also looks at mortality rates. The first six items address one main question: should you keep studying? Item 1 explains which options the law rules out. Item 2 explores how education affects lifespan. Item 3 shows what level of schooling most people in China have attained. Item 4 lists financial aid available when tuition is unaffordable. Item 5 describes alternatives if you don’t get into regular high school. Item 6 turns the “study versus work” dilemma into a simple calculation you can do yourself. The next seven items tackle another question: once you decide to learn something, how do you pick the right skill? Official statistics on
